evals.prompt: We need a new DangerButton because delete actions need a red button.
evals.expected_output: A Quick-mode decision that challenges the new component: REUSE Button if it already has a destructive intent, otherwise EXTEND Button with a semantic value such as intent=destructive. Unknown Tier 0 facts are marked unknown, naming is semantic rather than colour-based, and the delete screen is left alone.
expectations: Does not create DangerButton solely because the action is red.
Recommends REUSE or EXTEND of the existing Button with a semantic destructive intent (e.g., intent=destructive or the product's existing term) instead of a new component.
Does not propose a colour-named API such as red=true or color=red.
States that whether Button already has an intent/kind property is unknown without library or code evidence, and makes the REUSE vs EXTEND choice conditional on it.
Does not redesign the delete screen or specify the delete confirmation flow.
Does not produce an RFC, migration plan, changelog or governance process for this decision.
Reads at most one reference file (references/component-architecture-and-states.md).

evals.prompt: We found 87 hex values in the product. Convert all of them into design tokens.
evals.expected_output: A token audit plan, not a conversion: inventory each value's usage and context, normalize, cluster primitives, assign roles, classify (existing-token bypass, missing role, drift, intentional exception, unknown), then propose primitive and semantic layers and a migration map. Equal values with different roles stay separate.
expectations: Does not convert 87 values into 87 tokens or propose a one-to-one hex-to-token mapping.
Requires an inventory of where and how each value is used (component, property such as fill, text or border, use count) before naming tokens.
Separates primitive (raw palette) tokens from semantic role tokens and derives semantic names from roles, not from values.
Classifies values into categories that include existing-token bypass, missing role, accidental drift, intentional exception and unknown.
States that values that are equal but serve different roles remain separate semantic tokens.
Defers the migration mapping until after classification and gives no forecast of resulting token counts before the inventory exists.
Does not invent specific token names for the 87 values without usage evidence.

evals.prompt: Add compact, loading, icon-only, destructive, full-width, selected and mobile as boolean properties on Button.
evals.expected_output: A smaller semantic property model: each requested boolean classified as size, state, content model or family member, intent, layout, toggle state or responsive behaviour; mobile rejected; selected recognized as toggle semantics; invalid combinations named; Figma/code parity and breaking-change impact addressed.
expectations: Classifies each requested boolean into a dimension: compact as size, loading as state, icon-only as content model or IconButton, destructive as intent, full-width as layout, selected as toggle state, mobile as responsive behaviour.
Rejects mobile as a component property.
Identifies that selected changes semantics (toggle, aria-pressed or ToggleButton) rather than being a visual variant.
Separates states (loading, selected) from variants (intent, size).
Names at least two invalid or conflicting combinations (e.g., loading with disabled, icon-only without an accessible name) and how they are prevented or enforced.
Proposes a smaller model with enums for intent and size instead of seven independent booleans.
Checks Figma/code prop parity and flags folding existing booleans into enums as a breaking change that needs aliases or variant remapping.

evals.prompt: Use our existing Card, Button and Badge components to make this pricing screen cleaner and improve the hierarchy.
evals.expected_output: If the skill is invoked: a one-line routing to ui-visual-design, because composing a screen from existing Card, Button and Badge components is screen-level work. This skill re-engages only for a reusable design-system gap.
expectations: Routes the request to ui-visual-design as screen-level composition with existing components.
Does not propose new components, variants, properties or tokens.
Does not give layout, hierarchy, spacing or typography recommendations for the pricing screen.
States that this skill re-engages only for a reusable design-system gap ([DS GAP]) that the existing Card, Button or Badge cannot meet.
Reads no reference files.

evals.prompt: When file upload partially fails, should retry happen per file or for the whole batch?
evals.expected_output: If the skill is invoked: a one-line routing to interaction-design, because retry scope after a partial upload failure is a feature-specific interaction decision, not a reusable component property.
expectations: Routes the request to interaction-design as a feature-specific interaction decision.
Does not itself recommend per-file or whole-batch retry.
Does not add retry-related properties or states to a reusable FileUpload component.
Does not promote the decision into the design system; at most names reuse across features as the evidence that would make a reusable contract relevant.
Reads no reference files.

evals.prompt: Our Button has `intent=destructive` and `size=compact` in Figma, but the production Button component does not support those props. Audit the mismatch.
evals.expected_output: A design-system parity audit of Button: evidence from both sides, mismatches classified with a named source of truth per item, existing code equivalents checked, the smallest reconciliation with breaking-change status, and reusable accessibility implications of the compact size and destructive intent.
expectations: Treats the request as design-system parity between the Figma Button component and the production Button component, not as feature or staging QA.
Asks for or inspects both the Figma component properties and the production Button props or types (or Storybook) and marks missing evidence as unknown.
Checks whether production already expresses the same concepts under other names (e.g., kind=danger or size=sm) before recommending new props.
Classifies each mismatch (e.g., Figma ahead, unsupported Figma property, naming mismatch) and names a source of truth per item without assuming Figma is correct.
Recommends the smallest reconciliation per mismatch and states whether each change is breaking.
Notes reusable accessibility implications: the compact size against the WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 target-size minimum (24x24 CSS px or the spacing exception) and destructive-intent contrast per mode.
Does not assign release-blocking severities or write feature acceptance criteria.

evals.prompt: The checkout page is built on staging. Compare it against the approved Figma screens and tell me what should block release.
evals.expected_output: If the skill is invoked: a one-line routing to delivery-product-collaboration, because comparing a staging checkout build with approved screens and deciding release blockers is feature build QA. A specific reusable component or token mismatch found there can come back here.
expectations: Routes the request to delivery-product-collaboration as feature build vs approved design QA.
Does not compare the checkout screens or list implementation defects.
Does not decide what blocks release or assign severities.
States that a specific reusable component or token mismatch found during that QA can return to this skill as a system-parity question.
Does not load references/design-code-sync-and-quality.md for the checkout comparison.

evals.prompt: We want to rename `color.brand.primary` to `color.action.primary.background`. Can we just rename it in Figma?
evals.expected_output: Not a Figma-only rename: inventory consumers across Figma, code and docs; distinguish a rename from a semantic change (brand.primary may have non-action uses, so this may be a split); keep a deprecated alias during a compatibility window; state the breaking-change conditions.
expectations: Does not approve a Figma-only rename.
Requires inventorying consumers in Figma, code (including generated outputs or downstream packages) and documentation before renaming.
Distinguishes a pure rename from a semantic change and flags that color.brand.primary may have non-action consumers, so the change may be a split into separate roles.
Recommends keeping the old name as a deprecated alias pointing to the new token during a compatibility window.
States that removing the old name without an alias is breaking, while an aliased rename with an unchanged value is non-breaking.
Does not invent consumer counts.

evals.prompt: This campaign card needs a unique gradient that will never be reused. Should we add it to the core token system?
evals.expected_output: Keep the one-off gradient out of the core token system: document it as an intentional exception with reason, scope, owner and review date, and name the reuse evidence that would justify tokenizing it later.
expectations: Advises against adding the one-off campaign gradient to the core token system.
Recommends documenting it as an intentional exception with reason, scope, owner and a review or expiry date.
States the reuse evidence that would justify tokenizing it later.
Does not create a campaign mode, theme or component token.
Does not insist that every raw value must become a token.

evals.prompt: Do we already have a component for this pattern? If not, create one.
evals.expected_output: No invented inventory: state that whether a component exists cannot be confirmed without library or code evidence, ask what the pattern is, list the system sources to inspect, explain the REUSE > COMPOSE > EXTEND > CREATE sequence, and keep any recommendation conditional.
expectations: Does not claim that a matching component exists or does not exist.
Asks what the pattern is (purpose, anatomy or where it occurs) because none was described.
Lists the system evidence to inspect: library components with their properties and variants, tokens or variables, code components and props, Storybook and documentation.
Explains the REUSE > COMPOSE > EXTEND > CREATE order and that CREATE requires a repeated need and a distinct semantic purpose.
Does not create a new component, API or anatomy spec.
Keeps any recommendation explicitly conditional on the missing evidence.

evals.prompt: What states and keyboard/focus behavior must our reusable FileUpload component support across products?
evals.expected_output: A reusable FileUpload behaviour contract: states derived from behaviour, a keyboard/focus contract that does not depend on drag and drop, accessible names and status announcements, with feature-specific policy (retry scope, limits, copy) left to interaction-design.
expectations: Treats the request as a reusable component behaviour contract owned by this skill.
Derives the state set from behaviour, including focus-visible, disabled, drag-over, uploading or progress and error, with success only where the products use it.
Defines a keyboard/focus contract in which drag and drop is not the only input path (a keyboard-operable browse control or native file input) and focus is managed after files are added or removed.
Requires accessible names for per-file actions and status announcements for progress, completion and errors.
Leaves feature-specific policy such as per-file vs batch retry, file limits and error copy to interaction-design or product configuration.
Does not claim the component is accessible on the basis of automated checks.

evals.prompt: Storybook's accessibility addon shows zero violations for our Combobox. Can we mark it as 'accessible' in the design-system docs?
evals.expected_output: No 'accessible' label from automation alone: explain axe coverage limits and Incomplete results, note that WCAG 2.2 rules are opt-in in the default ruleset, list manual checks proportional to a Combobox, and propose accurate documentation wording.
expectations: Does not approve labelling the Combobox 'accessible' or 'conformant' from automated results alone.
Explains that automated checks cover only part of WCAG issues and that Incomplete results require manual review.
Notes that the addon's default ruleset covers WCAG 2.0/2.1 A and AA and that WCAG 2.2 rules must be enabled or checked manually.

Lists manual checks proportional to a Combobox: keyboard interaction model, focus management, screen-reader announcements on at least one desktop and one mobile assistive technology, zoom/reflow and forced colours.
Proposes accurate documentation wording, such as no automated violations under a named ruleset with manual validation pending.
